claims.text: Random distributions of multiple atomic species in refractory high-entropy alloys produce severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion produces wavy dislocation lines.
The wavy dislocation lines impede the mobility of <111>{110} edge dislocations.
The proposed dislocation behavior is responsible for the alloy's nearly isotropic room-temperature elastic response.
The proposed dislocation behavior moderates the increase in elastic anisotropy at elevated temperatures.
NbTaTiV can be prepared as a single-phase BCC solid solution by arc melting, homogenization, and water cooling.
The NbTaTiV alloy remains a single BCC solid solution up to 900°C.
Compressive and in situ neutron-diffraction testing of NbTaTiV has been performed at room temperature, 500°C, 700°C, and 900°C at a strain rate of 1×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹.
Fluctuating atomic sizes create local lattice distortions that shift edge-dislocation core positions away from ideal slip planes.
Displaced edge-dislocation cores result in wavy dislocation lines and reduced dislocation mobility.
Reduced dislocation mobility underlies the intrinsic ductility of the alloy.
NbTaTiV exhibits a nearly isotropic elastic response at room temperature.
Elastic anisotropy in NbTaTiV increases gradually at elevated temperatures.
The elevated-temperature increase in NbTaTiV elastic anisotropy is modest relative to conventional BCC alloys.
NbTaTiV has lower yield strength than conventional BCC alloys under identical conditions.
Screw dislocations typically dominate deformation in conventional BCC alloys.
Conventional BCC alloys show a greater temperature-dependent evolution of elastic anisotropy than NbTaTiV.
Reducing the number of constituent elements reduces compositional fluctuations and lattice distortion.
Reducing compositional fluctuations should alter dislocation behavior, mechanical properties, and thermoelastic response.
